status: LOCKED - parameters frozen before any result on this dataset was inspected
hypothesis: Time-series momentum persists in GBPUSD over multi-day horizons. A Donchian breakout in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend, held with an ATR-scaled stop and a shorter-channel trailing exit, should capture it. Trading infrequently on H4 keeps transaction cost small relative to risk per trade.

why_these_parameters.timeframe_minutes: H4. Chosen from cost arithmetic, not fitting: at a ~1.3 pip round trip, a ~60 pip ATR stop puts cost at ~2% of risk. The v14 scalps put it at ~26%, which research/v14_4_cost_stress_report.py shows is fatal.
why_these_parameters.entry_lookback: 20 - the classic Turtle/Donchian breakout length, taken as published.
why_these_parameters.exit_lookback: 10 - the classic Turtle trailing exit, half the entry length.
why_these_parameters.atr_period: 14 - the standard Wilder period, already the default in sizing.py.
why_these_parameters.atr_stop_mult: 2.0 - matches AtrConfig.sl_mult in sizing.py; not re-tuned.

provenance: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics. Donchian channel breakout as popularised by the Turtle traders. No parameter was selected by searching this dataset.
note_on_trials: This candidate is a single pre-registered specification. If any parameter is later changed in response to a result, the trial count must rise and the deflated Sharpe must be recomputed against the new count - see mt5_ai_bridge/validation.py.
honest_limitation: The only price data committed to this repository is GBPUSD_M5.csv, roughly eight months of M5 bars (2025-10-28 to 2026-06-30). Resampled to H4 that is about 1,000 bars, which cannot produce the 200 out-of-sample trades the gates require. A verdict on this candidate needs several years of history that is not currently in the repo.
